source.title: PADDLES: Phase-Amplitude Spectrum Disentangled Early Stopping for Learning with Noisy Labels
source.authors: Huaxi Huang; Hui-Sung Kang; Sheng Liu; Olivier Salvado; Thierry Rakotoarivelo; Dadong Wang; Tong-Liang Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study measures test accuracy under several types and levels of label corruption and compares training behavior across image components. It does not apply the original random-label experiment.
record.gate_note: The study does not report results for completely random labels, unstructured inputs, or explicit regularization. The paper's discussion of learning real patterns before noise cites prior work; it is not extracted as this study's result. Table 1 and Table 2 report test accuracies for PADDLES under corrupted-label conditions, but not training error.
record.test_reason: The study's own clean-label and noisy-label training-loss curves bear on V6 in a frequency-spectrum setting. Section 3.2 explicitly attributes clean-label fitting before noisy-label overfitting to Figure 1. The extracted benchmark accuracies measure the proposed mitigation method's performance and do not test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that phase-spectrum learning is more resistant to label noise than amplitude-spectrum learning, and that separate stopping combined with progressive early stopping improves noisy-label classification.
record.recipe_differences: PADDLES detaches amplitude and phase spectrum gradients at different training times and incorporates progressive early stopping; the experiments use synthetic and real-world noisy labels rather than the original random-label intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that outcomes vary with label-noise type and level, disentangle position, and the AS and PS stopping points.

fits_no_version.finding: Tables 1 and 2 report PADDLES test accuracies after sample selection and supervised or semi-supervised noisy-label learning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Separately stopping amplitude- and phase-spectrum learning improves robustness to noisy labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Amplitude- and phase-spectrum inputs differ in noisy-label fitting speed, with phase-spectrum learning more resistant to noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input frequency representation affects the rate of noisy-label memorization.

record.code_released: Codes will be available upon acceptance.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
record.problems: The extracted tables report test accuracy but not training error; the key spectral comparisons are presented in figures. No experiment uses completely random labels or the all-corrupted endpoint described by V4.
record.rows_left_out: Other methods' benchmark scores, CIFAR-N and Clothing-1M results, ablations, and text-dataset results are not extracted because those conditions do not report the random-corruption test accuracy named by V4. Figures 1 and 7 report spectral training curves and test accuracy but do not provide extractable numeric values for the required training-error claim.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random labels to zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged training hyperparameters.
Time to fit random versus true labels and convergence slowdown across corruption fractions. Table 7 compares methods at one noise level instead.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training-set fitting across a clean-to-completely-corrupted sweep and steadily rising test error toward chance.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent random-label fitting and whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Fully random labeling and generality beyond the tested models, datasets, and input representations.

missing.what: Add qualitative V6 rows for clean versus noisy subset loss trajectories in the Figure 1 experiment. Although rows_left_out mentions these curves, its rationale wrongly requires V4 training-error numbers and overlooks their direct evidence for V6; Section 3.2 explicitly reports the temporal ordering as this study's result.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly treats clean-before-noise learning solely as a citation to prior work. The introduction cites Arpit, but Section 3.2 also grounds this behavior in the study's own Figure 1. Exact curve values are unavailable in the supplied text, so the V6 verdict rests on the authors' explicit qualitative interpretation. None of R1–R20 supplies evidence for a claim-version verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, zero or near-zero training error, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training time to fit random versus true labels and convergence time as corruption increases.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.

Whether training error remains perfect across corruption levels, a clean-to-all-corrupted sweep, and whether test error rises steadily toward chance. The reported test accuracies are extracted, but the study does not report the training-error measure named by this version.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation affect fitting random labels or generalization on true labels.
Whether the same network learns real-label patterns before memorizing noisy or random labels.

relationships.condition: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 with 50% symmetric label noise
relationships.reason: Based on Figure 1 and Section 3.2, rather than R1–R20: the authors report clean-label fitting before later noisy-label overfitting, using separate subset loss curves.
relationships.display_finding: Separate subset loss curves showed clean-label fitting before later noisy-label overfitting.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
